html:
The Ramayana is one of the two great Sanskrit epics of India, a poem of about 24,000 verses credited to the sage Valmiki. Its oldest parts may go back to about 500 BCE, and it reached its present form by about 300 CE.

It tells the story of Rama, prince of Ayodhya. He is sent into exile in the forest for fourteen years with his wife Sita and his brother Lakshmana. The demon king Ravana carries Sita off to Lanka. Rama, helped by the monkey general Hanuman and his army, builds a bridge to the island, kills Ravana and comes home to be crowned.

Rama became the model of the just king and Sita of the faithful wife, and Rama came to be worshipped as a form of the god Vishnu. The festival of Diwali marks his return home.

The story was retold in almost every language of South and Southeast Asia: Kamban's version in Tamil, the Ramcharitmanas in Hindi, the Ramakien in Thailand, the reliefs at Prambanan in Java. With the Mahabharata it is the most widely known story in India.
